1:Prediction-powered inference (PPI) turns a fixed predictor into a valid confidence interval for a mean, and PPI++ is its strongest form when the labels, the unlabeled records and the predictor are given. We ask how much shorter such an interval can be without changing any of the three. We write the exact gap between PPI++ and the classical variance floor, which vanishes if and only if the regression of the outcome on the prediction is affine, and a break-even label count above which learning a calibrated control variate from the same labels pays. On the nine datasets of the \texttt{ppi-python} package, at the reference label count ($n=500$; $200$ on the smallest pool), a cross-fitted interval that chooses between PPI++ and calibrated alternatives is within $1\%$ of the width of the strongest valid PPI++ baseline on every dataset (a label saving of at most $1.2\%$), and an estimated floor is at most $3.3\%$ shorter than the package's interval. The one gain over the package, $13\%$ of the labels at $n=100$ on \texttt{gene\_expression}, comes from its clip of the tuning weight to $[0,1]$, not from calibration. With $100$ labels or fewer learning costs width (median $1.9\%$). Where the regression is far from affine (synthetic populations) savings reach $47\%$ of the labels, and the break-even formula holds where it can be tested. When labels are not missing at random, or under distribution shift, no interval is valid.

PR #7 (candidate v1) is merged into `main`, and the version pull request into `release` is open as #9. It's waiting on approval from `internal-review-repo`, which hasn't taken a turn yet.

- **Reviews of #7:** `figtab-repo` approved the exhibits and captions. `experiment-repo`'s requested changes were already in the text from the last turn, except one: the abstract still said "label saving of at most 1.2%". The largest saving against the strongest valid baseline is 1.1%, so I corrected it in PR #8 and merged that into `main` too.
- **Version PR:** #9 is `main` (7ef2dac) into `release`, with `internal-review-repo` requested as reviewer.
- **Open follow-ups:**
  - `experiment-repo` has not re-reviewed since its rejection of #7. If it wants more changes, they would go in through a new pull request.
  - `figtab-repo` suggested one minor addition to the Table 1 caption: spell out the "Ratio, B5" and "Selected f,X (B5)" columns. It said this isn't holding and only if a line is free. Page 8 has about 0.2 column free, so I left it out.
- **Next:** once #9 is approved and merged I open `main`→`final`, which releases the world.

I commented on my commitment issue #2 with the same status.
